name: EASTGROUP PROPERTIES, INC.
sector: Real Estate / Industrial REIT (shallow-bay, Sun Belt)
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow 5/10: infill shallow-bay scarcity in Sun Belt markets, demonstrated rent pricing power (leasing spreads +34% GAAP / +19% cash, cash same-store NOI +8-9%) and a development channel that creates assets at a ~9.4% stabilized yield give EastGroup more than a generic landlord's moat, but the assets remain replicable with capital, there is no lock-in beyond leases, growth is bought with continuous equity issuance (shares +7.3%/yr), and filed ROE has run only 6.9-7.7% in the last three years with roic_proxy not computable from the REIT presentation — not the sustained well-above-cost-of-capital record a 7+ requires. In line with KIM (5) and above the generic REIT 4s (AMH, AHR, MAA, INVH) on the strength of the development alpha and spreads.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 7.3%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md

CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED: the only cash tag filed for the latest fiscal year is the combined cash + restricted-cash total and no restricted-cash tag separates it — net debt is UNDERSTATED by the restricted amount (escrow / collateral / regulatory); check the balance sheet before trusting HIGH_NET_DEBT's absence
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-11, accession 0000049600-26-000010), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Capital improvements' (us-gaap PaymentsForCapitalImprovements): $(51,116) thousand for FY2023, $(59,288) thousand for FY2024 and $(75,830) thousand for FY2025; the override value is the median of the three filed years (the FY2024 figure). Cross-checked against statements.json, whose capex series is exactly this line.); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
one_liner: Quality Sun Belt industrial REIT, moat 5/10 — even on the generous TTM base ($8.09/sh) the weighted IRR is 7.6% (weighted IV@15% $78.55 vs the $197.44 price), the bear→bull band is Tier D (even the super-bull scenario, 11.01%, reaches only the C band), and the price would have to fall to ~$79 to clear the 15% hurdle; confidence low (sector model mismatch).
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Infill shallow-bay locations in supply-constrained Sun Belt markets: zoning/permit friction and scarce infill land make the 65.8M sq ft portfolio hard to replicate at any price near book; quarter-end occupancy 95.6%, same-store 96.9% (Q2 2026)
Demonstrated pricing power: Q2 2026 leasing spreads +34% GAAP / +19% cash on a record 3.9M sq ft signed; cash same-store NOI +8.3% in Q2, +8.8% YTD

Development alpha: self-developed projects transfer at a ~9.4% stabilized yield (management, Q2 2026 coverage), well above acquisition cap rates — a structural cost advantage over REITs that must buy growth
Balance sheet as a competitive weapon: debt/total market cap 12.9%, debt/EBITDA 3.0x, coverage 15.1x, no revolver drawn ($675M available) at Q2 2026 — cheap, always-available capital through cycles
Diversified rent roll (top 10 tenants 6.6% of rents) and 186 consecutive quarterly dividends; FFO/share compounded ~10.7%/yr over five years (peer coverage)
moat_against: Real estate is replicable with capital — no network effects; tenant lock-in is a multi-year lease, and shallow-bay space competes with new build-for-rent industrial supply

Filed returns are moderate, not wide-moat: ROE 9.5% (FY2022) → 7.7% (FY2023) → 6.9% (FY2024) → 7.4% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json; roic_proxy and gross margin are not computable from the filed REIT presentation — no record of returns durably well above the cost of capital
Growth is equity-funded: share count CAGR 7.3%/yr, issuance proceeds $692,312,000 (FY2023), $717,659,000 (FY2024), $264,071,000 (FY2025) — per-share economics lag portfolio growth

Sun Belt concentration (Florida, Texas, Arizona, California) and a post-COVID industrial supply wave in several markets cap rent growth as the 34% leasing spreads normalize; same-property NOI guidance (+6.8% for 2026) is already below the +8.8% YTD print
Development is cyclical: the $487M pipeline (17 projects, 3.2M sq ft) must lease up through whatever demand does next; development starts guidance was cut one quarter and raised the next in 2026
